_about: The holiness hub (plan 7.6f), the fourth after love, righteousness and peace, built to the same level. Holiness is one family in the Hebrew and Greek -- קָדוֹשׁ and ἅγιος (holy), קֹדֶשׁ (holiness, the holy place, holy things), קָדַשׁ and ἁγιάζω (to make holy), מִקְדָּשׁ (sanctuary), ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης, ἁγιωσύνη (holiness, sanctification) -- and the English renders it holy, sanctify, consecrate, dedicate, sacred, sanctuary and saints. The committee (2026-10-09) flagged it medium: ἅγιος is mostly the Spirit's title (89 of 222 verses), and how the saints come to be holy is argued by Wesleyan, Pentecostal, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers. So: the rows are split by who or what is called holy; 'the Holy Spirit' and 'the Holy One' are by hand; 'saints' is kept as the Berean writes it; the contested point is set out as rows side by side. The Hebrew nouns sit under the noun form and the Greek adjective under the adjective form -- the grammar, not a different sense; the hub is the whole family. Rows as in love.json and righteousness.json; match 'all'. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py. Consolidated 2026-10-10 from 43 rows to 26 (coordinator: about 15-25 by the brief): rows that say the same thing were merged by what the text makes holy; small rows fold into the 'Every other use' rows. Every verse stays placed. Panel fixes 2026-10-10 ('ship after fixes'): the two sanctification verb rows made one with no done/ongoing split; framing words out of the noun pair; one no-side note in all places; the Holy One row split into the Hebrew and the New Testament; the saints verses gathered; labels brought into the verses' own words.

titles.adjective: Who and what is called holy
titles.noun: Holiness, the holy place and holy things

_words_why: The family in both testaments: קָדוֹשׁ and Aramaic קַדִּישׁ with ἅγιος (the Greek Old Testament renders qodesh and qadosh by ἅγιος, and the LXX of Daniel the Aramaic), קֹדֶשׁ, מִקְדָּשׁ, קָדַשׁ with ἁγιάζω, and the Greek nouns ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης, ἁγιωσύνη. Left out as different words: קֶדֶשׁ and קָדֵשׁ the places Kedesh and Kadesh, קָדֵשׁ the temple prostitute (the same letters, another word), and ὅσιος, ὁσιότης, ἁγνός, ἱερός, דְּבִיר -- the English also says 'holy', 'sacred' or 'sanctuary' for them; they are named apart below.
_sense_why: Empty: every use of these words is in the concept's range -- holy, sanctuary, sacred donations, dedicated gifts, saints, consecrate, set apart -- the Berean's glosses for one word. Nothing is dropped by the English; the rows divide the uses by what is holy.

others._why: Words the English renders holy, sacred, sanctify, sanctuary or saint that are not this family: ὅσιος 'holy One' (Acts 2:27, 13:35; Rev 16:5), ὁσιότης 'holiness' (Luke 1:75, Eph 4:24), דְּבִיר 'sanctuary' (the inner room of Solomon's temple), נֵזֶר 'consecration' (the Nazirite's hair), ἱερός 'sacred' Scriptures. Named apart with their verses; the reader is never handed one as the other. h4993 is a gloss stray; h4676 מַצֵּבָה is a pagan 'sacred pillar' and is no help to a reader of holiness. חָסִיד (h2623), the faithful or loyal ones, which the Berean prints 'saints' in 16 of its 32 verses, is added by hand (others.add) with those verses first and a note: the gloss rule matches MACULA's gloss ('faithful'), not the Berean's English, so it could not find them. Panel fix 2026-10-10: Ps 16:10 (the Berean's 'Your Holy One') added to the חָסִיד verses, and Acts 2:27 and 13:35 put first under ὅσιος with a note that they quote it.
others.title: Other words translated “holy”, “saints”, “sacred”, “sanctuary”

h2623.note: Another word, חָסִיד, “faithful, godly”; the Berean prints “saints” in sixteen of its verses (listed here) and “Your Holy One” in Psalm 16:10, which Acts 2:27 and 13:35 quote with the Greek ὅσιος (listed under that word).

g3741.note: Acts 2:27 and 13:35 quote Psalm 16:10, where the Hebrew is חָסִיד (listed above); the Greek here is ὅσιος.

Hos.12.1.why: the Hebrew's Hos 12:1 ('faithful to the Holy One') is printed in the Berean's 11:12; its 12:1 is the verse about Ephraim and the wind

1Sam.21.5.why: the lexicon numbers the Hebrew verses 21:5-7 where the Berean has 21:4-6: 'there is some consecrated bread' is the Berean's 21:4

1Sam.21.6.why: as 1Sam 21:5 above: the Hebrew's 21:6 ('the bodies of the young men are holy') is the Berean's 21:5

1Sam.21.7.why: as 1Sam 21:5 above: the Hebrew's 21:7 ('the priest gave him the holy bread') is the Berean's 21:6; the Berean's 21:7 is Doeg

rows.label: “The LORD our God is holy”, “Holy Father”, “Holy is His name”; “Be holy, because I am holy”
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 2 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "Be holy, because I am holy"; "“The LORD our God is holy”, “Holy Father”, “Holy is His name”". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order. Both say the LORD's holiness in the text's own words; the divine persons stay by pick. Earlier notes: by hand: the verses where the LORD says it of Himself (Leviticus) and where Peter writes it as quoted; Lev 20:7 says 'be holy, because I am the LORD your God' and stands under 'A holy people' | by hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself says the LORD, God, the Father, or the One whose name is Holy (Isa 57:15; Luke 1:49 'the Mighty One ... Holy is His name') is holy. Ps 22:3 and 99:3 speak to Him ('You are holy', 'He is holy') in psalms that name Him. 'Lord, holy and true' (Rev 6:10) and 'the One who is holy and true' (Rev 3:7) say only the title and stand in the row after next

rows.label: The LORD, “the Holy One of Israel”
rows.note: The text also says “the Holy One of Jacob” (Isa 29:23), “the Holy One in Israel” (Ezek 39:7), “my Holy One” (Hab 1:12) and “the Holy One among you” (Hos 11:9); in each the LORD or God is named in the verse.
rows._why: by hand: every verse where the title stands with the LORD or God named in it. Isaiah's thirty uses are the bulk

rows.label: “The Holy One”: the title without a name
rows.note: The verse gives the title and no name.
rows._why: the righteousness hub's 'He is righteous' row, for the same reason: the text says only the title. Hos 11:12 is the Berean's verse for the Hebrew's 12:1 (see moves) Panel fix 2026-10-10: split: the six Hebrew verses are heard as the Hebrew's 'the Holy One' first, not under Revelation's 'holy and true'.

rows.label: Jesus called holy
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: verses where the text itself names Jesus holy -- 'Your holy servant Jesus' (Acts 4:27, 4:30), 'Jesus of Nazareth ... the Holy One of God' (Mark 1:24, Luke 4:34, said by an unclean spirit), 'You are the Holy One of God' (John 6:69, said to Jesus), 'the Holy and Righteous One' (Acts 3:14, of Jesus named in 3:13), the Holy One to be born (Luke 1:35, to Mary, who is told in 1:31 to name Him Jesus). Acts 2:27 and 13:35 'Your Holy One' are the different word ὅσιος and stand with the other words, not here Panel fix 2026-10-10: the note says who speaks, so the row does not read as testimony the page offers.
rows.note: Said of Jesus by an unclean spirit (Mark 1:24, Luke 4:34), by Peter (John 6:69), in Peter's sermon (Acts 3:14), in the church's prayer (Acts 4:27, 4:30) and by the angel to Mary (Luke 1:35).

rows.label: “from the Holy One”, “the One who is holy and true”, “Lord, holy and true”
rows.note: The verse gives the title and no name. Some readers take it of the Father and some of Christ; the page does not choose.
rows._why: Split from the Holy One row (panel fix 2026-10-10): the New Testament verses, with the existing no-choice note. Doug, 2026-10-10: 'keep all 5' -- the page does not choose (as righteousness's 'He is righteous'); Luke 1:35, John 6:69, Acts 3:14 stay in 'Jesus called holy' and Isa 49:7 in the LORD's row on the same decision.

rows.label: “The Holy Spirit”
rows.note: In these verses the text calls the Spirit holy (“the Holy Spirit”). They are grouped here by that name. Where the noun is used instead -- “the spirit of Your holiness”, “the Spirit of holiness” -- see the noun section.
rows._why: by hand: the committee (2026-10-09) flagged that ἅγιος is mostly the Spirit's title and 'misleads' as holiness. 89 Greek verses where ἅγιος stands beside πνεῦμα (plus Eph 1:13, where the adjective follows the noun 'of promise'). Rom 15:19 is left out: the original has ἅγιος there (the Berean's 'the Spirit of God' follows another manuscript line) and a row labelled 'Holy Spirit' would show a verse without the words Panel fix 2026-10-10: the note no longer rules on how to read the word 'holy' (the panel: the earlier sentence read as setting the Spirit's holiness aside); it says what the text says and how the verses are grouped.

rows.label: “holy ones”, “the saints of the Most High”; “holy angels”
rows.note: The text says “holy ones”, “saints” and “holy angels”. Where the verse names angels (Mark 8:38, Luke 9:26, Acts 10:22, Rev 14:10) or the context does (Dan 4:13, 4:17, 4:23, 8:13) they are angels; where it says only “holy ones” or “saints” the page does not choose between heavenly beings and the LORD's people. Readers part on Daniel 7 and on 1 Thessalonians 3:13 above all.
rows._why: 'holy angels' are named as angels; the rest say 'holy ones' and the verse alone does not settle who. Dan 4:13, 4:17, 4:23 are the Aramaic 'a watcher, a holy one'; Dan 7 the Aramaic 'saints of the Most High' Panel fix 2026-10-10: the heading no longer leads with 'holy angels', which tilted every verse that way; 2 Thess 1:10 ('glorified in His saints ... by all who have believed, including you') names believers and moves to the saints row.

rows.label: Called holy: a people, a nation, “the Holy People”, “the holy seed”; priests, the Nazirite; a holy man, holy women, holy prophets and apostles
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 3 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "A holy people, a holy nation"; "Priests, Levites and the Nazirite, holy to the LORD"; "A holy man, holy prophets and apostles, holy women". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order.  Earlier notes: by hand: where a people is called holy by the adjective. Num 16:3 is Korah's claim, kept as the text's own words. The Hebrew noun's 'My holy people' is the noun section's Panel fix 2026-10-10: label renamed (it said 'holy to the LORD' of verses that are Herod's opinion and Korah's claim, and left out the holy women of 1 Pet 3:5); the Hebrew noun's five verses added so the Hebrew naming of Israel as holy is not hidden by the part-of-speech split.
rows.note: Num 16:3 is Korah's claim; Mark 6:20 is said of John by the narrator. “My holy people”, “the Holy People” and “the holy seed” (Exod 22:31, Isa 62:12, Isa 6:13, Ezra 9:2, Dan 12:7) are the Hebrew noun קֹדֶשׁ and also stand under “Every other use” in the noun section.

rows.label: “Called to be saints”, “called to be holy”, “chose us ... to be holy”, “a holy calling”, “present you holy”, “holy and beloved”, “holy brothers”
rows.note: Christian traditions part on how and when the saints are made holy. The page sets the text's verses side by side and takes no side. A verse that fits more than one stands in more than one.
rows._why: Wesleyan, Pentecostal, Reformed, Catholic and Orthodox readers argue how saints come to be holy (committee, 2026-10-09). The labels are the text's own words ('called to be saints', 'chose us ... to be holy', 'present you holy') Panel fix 2026-10-10: label fitted to all eight verses (four of them say 'present her/you holy', 'holy and beloved', 'holy brothers', not 'called' or 'chosen'); the no-side note now has one wording in all places and names no positions.

rows.label: The saints: written to, greeted, served, loved, prayed for and interceded for; their inheritance, the faith and the mystery given them; judging; harmed, killed, praying, enduring
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 2 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "Letters to the saints: greetings to and from them; serving, loving and praying for them"; "The saints in Acts and Revelation: harmed, killed, praying, enduring". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order.  Earlier notes: 'saints' kept as the Berean writes it for ἅγιοι, 'holy ones' (committee: 'keep saints phrases as written') Panel fix 2026-10-10: the seventeen 'saints' verses left in 'Every other use' (1 Cor 6:2, Eph 1:18, Rom 8:27, Col 1:12, Rev 19:8 ...) plus 2 Thess 1:10 are the same word in the same sense; the label is widened to them. Matt 27:52 ('many saints ... raised') stays in the catch-all.

rows.label: A holy place, holy ground, the holy city, the holy mountain, the holy temple
rows._why: the adjective for a place: Hebrew קָדוֹשׁ 'in a holy place', Greek ἅγιος 'the holy city' and τὰ ἅγια ('the Holy Place'; Heb 8:2, 9:12, 9:24, 9:25, 10:19, 13:11 are 'holy places' in the Berean, the sanctuary). The Hebrew noun קֹדֶשׁ ('holy mountain', 'holy place', 'holy ground') is under the noun form below; this is the grammar, not a different sense Panel fix 2026-10-10: Hebrew examples first, and a note that the Greek verses use the words of the church and of heaven.
rows.note: The first ten are the Hebrew's “holy place”; the rest are the Greek, where the holy place, the holy city and the temple are also used of the church (1 Cor 3:17, Eph 2:21) and of the sanctuary in heaven (Heb 8:2, 9:24).

rows.label: Every other use
The LORD's holiness and what is His called holy: “majestic in holiness”, “My holy name”, His holy arm, covenant, word, throne, land, way; the Way of Holiness
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 3 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "“Majestic in holiness”, “the splendor of holiness”, “sworn by My holiness”, the Way of Holiness"; "What is the LORD's is called holy: His arm, covenant, word, throne, heaven, land, way"; "“My holy name”, “His holy name”". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order.  Earlier notes: by hand: the nine verses where the Berean prints the abstract 'holiness' for קֹדֶשׁ, all of the LORD's but the Way of Holiness | by the phrase (the name beside קֹדֶשׁ); 1 Chr 16:35 and Ps 106:47 are among the nine verses the lexicon's occurrence list leaves out, so the row is a list

rows.label: Holiness: “share in His holiness”, “sanctified by the Spirit”, Christ “our holiness”
rows.note: Christian traditions part on how and when the saints are made holy. The page sets the text's verses side by side and takes no side. A verse that fits more than one stands in more than one.
rows._why: ἁγιασμός, ἁγιότης (Greek nouns); picked by what each verse ties holiness to -- God, the Spirit, Christ -- and not by the Berean's rendering 'sanctification' or 'holiness', which differ for the same word Panel fix 2026-10-10: 'that is God's' dropped; the panel found the two labels lined up as given-by-God against pursued-by-us, which is the very point the traditions argue, and the sort did not hold on that line (1 Thess 3:13 and 4:7 are God's doing and stood on the other side).

rows.label: Holiness: “pursue holiness”, “perfecting holiness”, “leads to holiness”, “called ... to holiness”
rows.note: Christian traditions part on how and when the saints are made holy. The page sets the text's verses side by side and takes no side. A verse that fits more than one stands in more than one.
rows._why: the other side of the contested point, from the same Greek nouns; ἁγιωσύνη (2 Cor 7:1, 1 Thess 3:13) is 'holiness' in the Berean as ἁγιασμός is Panel fix 2026-10-10: 'aim and fruit of the life' dropped, as above.

rows.label: “Your Holy Spirit”, “the Spirit of holiness”
rows.note: The Hebrew says “the spirit of Your holiness”; Romans 1:4 says “the Spirit of holiness”. The 89 verses that say “the Holy Spirit” with the adjective are in the first section.
rows._why: by hand: the noun, not the adjective, is used; the builder files them by part of speech

rows.label: The sanctuary and the Holy Place, the Most Holy Place and the most holy things, holy ground; the holy mountain, city, temple, dwelling
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 3 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "The Most Holy Place, the most holy things"; "The sanctuary, the holy place, holy ground"; "The holy mountain, the holy city, the holy temple, the holy dwelling". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order. The Most Holy row was a rule (קֹדֶשׁ beside קֹדֶשׁ) and the mountain row a rule (with הַר, עִיר, הֵיכָל, מָעוֹן); now lists. Dan 9:26 stays in the sanctuary list and out of 'holy city', as before. Earlier notes: the Hebrew's superlative is the word repeated ('holy of holies'): קֹדֶשׁ beside קֹדֶשׁ, by the phrase, not by the Berean's rendering | מִקְדָּשׁ (all 72 verses) and the Berean's 'sanctuary', 'Holy Place' and 'holy ground' for קֹדֶשׁ, as an explicit list: the lexicon's occurrence list leaves out Lev 10:4, 16:17 and Ezek 44:7, which only a pick can place. The 'sanctuary shekel' verses, a measure, are left to the last row

rows.label: What is made holy: days, garments, oil, offerings, dedicated gifts, the holy portion; “HOLY TO THE LORD”; “between the holy and the common”
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 4 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "Holy days: the Sabbath, the sacred assemblies, the Jubilee"; "Holy things: garments, anointing oil, offerings, dedicated gifts, the holy portion"; "“HOLY TO THE LORD”"; "“Between the holy and the common”". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order. Holy days was a rule (with מִקְרָא, שַׁבָּת, יוֹם, חַג); now a list. Earlier notes: the Berean's 'holy things', 'sacred donations', 'dedicated gifts', 'votive gifts', 'holy garments', 'sacred anointing oil' and 'holy portion' for קֹדֶשׁ, as a list: first found by the garment, oil and offering words beside it (בֶּגֶד, מִשְׁחָה, שֶׁמֶן, נֵזֶר, תְּרוּמָה, כְּלִי, אוֹצָר), then added by the Berean's own renderings | by the phrase in the Berean: 'holy to the LORD', 'holy to you', 'set apart to the LORD'. The plate on the high priest's forehead, and what Zechariah says will carry it | Ezek 42:20 and 44:23 carry the word in the Hebrew, but the lexicon's occurrence list does not hold them, so they are picked

not_verses.Lev.10.10: 'unclean', the adjective, beside 'the common'; nothing is profaned

rows.label: Every other use
Who sanctifies: “I am the LORD who sanctifies you”; Jesus, “for them I sanctify Myself”, “by His own blood”
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 2 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "God sanctifies: “I am the LORD who sanctifies you”"; "Jesus sanctifies: “for them I sanctify Myself”, “by His own blood”". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order. Both lists stay by hand, as the divine persons are; only the row is shared. Earlier notes: by hand, as the divine persons are: the verses where the LORD, God or the Father is the one who sanctifies, in the verse or in the speech it belongs to (Num 3:13, 8:17, 1 Kgs 9:3, 7, 2 Chr 7:16, 20 are His own first-person words) | by hand: Heb 2:11 and 13:12 name Jesus; John 17:19 is His prayer ('Myself'); Eph 5:26 is Christ, named in 5:25, whom the verb's frame gives as the subject Panel fix 2026-10-10: a who-acts note, because in one row the two lists read as one agent. For Doug: Eph 5:26 and Heb 2:11 are placed with Jesus because of 5:25 and the name in 2:11; John 10:36 is the Father sanctifying Jesus.
rows.note: In each verse the text names who sanctifies: the LORD or the Father in the Old Testament verses and in 1 Thess 5:23; Jesus in John 17:19 and Heb 13:12 (and Eph 5:26, in the sentence that begins at 5:25). At Heb 2:11 the Berean prints “Jesus” where the Greek says only “He”; Jesus is named at 2:9. John 10:36 has the Father sanctifying Jesus. For the Spirit, see “Sanctified by”.
rows._doug: 2026-10-10, Doug: 'keep all 5' -- Eph 5:26 and Heb 2:11 stay with Jesus, by 5:25 and 2:9; the note says the Berean supplies the name at 2:11

rows.label: Hallow the name, regard the LORD as holy, “sanctify Christ as Lord”; “I will show Myself holy”
rows.note: 1 Pet 3:15, “sanctify Christ as Lord”, takes up the words of Isa 8:13, “The LORD of Hosts is the One you shall regard as holy”.
rows._doug: 2026-10-10, Doug: 'keep all 5' -- 1 Pet 3:15 stays beside Isa 8:13; the note says only that Peter uses Isaiah's phrase, and Isaiah's verse keeps its own words

rows.label: Consecrate and set apart: yourselves, the priests, the altar, the tabernacle, the house; the firstborn, a field, gifts; keep the Sabbath day holy
rows._why: Merged 2026-10-10 from 3 rows (consolidation to 26; the coordinator's rule: about 15-25): "Consecrate yourselves; consecrate the priests, the altar, the tabernacle, the house"; "Set apart to the LORD: the firstborn, a house, a field, gifts"; "Keep the Sabbath day holy". Every verse of the old rows is kept, as an explicit list in the Bible's order. Keep the Sabbath day holy was a rule (in verse with שַׁבָּת); now a list. Exod 20:11, 31:13 and Ezek 20:12 (the LORD made the Sabbath holy, the LORD who sanctifies) were taken back out: they say who sanctifies, not 'keep the Sabbath day holy'; they stay in 'Who sanctifies'.

rows.label: Sanctified by: the truth, the word, faith, “the blood of goats and bulls” (the old rites), “His own blood”, “the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ”, the Spirit, a believing spouse; “food sanctified by the word of God and prayer”
rows._why: by what each verse names as the means, in its own words; the page does not rank them. 1 Cor 7:14 ('sanctified through his believing wife') is here because the verse says 'sanctified' and names a means; the label says so; readers part on what it shows of the children (it is also a point in the baptism debates) and the page says nothing of that Panel fix 2026-10-10: the 'blood' label hid that Heb 9:13 is the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer, the old rites; 1 Tim 4:5 is food, not a person.

rows.label: “you were sanctified”, “we have been sanctified”, “those who are being sanctified”, “sanctify you completely”, “may be sanctified by the truth”, “let the holy continue to be holy”
rows.note: Christian traditions part on how and when the saints are made holy. The page sets the text's verses side by side and takes no side. A verse that fits more than one stands in more than one.
rows._why: Merged from "Having been sanctified, you were sanctified" (8) and "Being sanctified, sanctify you completely, let the holy continue to be holy" (5). Panel fix 2026-10-10: the panel found that the split into 'done' and 'ongoing' was not by the Greek form (John 17:19 and 1 Cor 1:2 are the same form on opposite sides), that the first label's quoted phrase was in none of its verses, and that the grouping was itself a reading. One row, in the Bible's order, labelled only in phrases the verses carry (1 Cor 6:11 'you were sanctified'; Heb 10:10 'we have been sanctified'; Heb 10:14 'those who are being sanctified'; 1 Thess 5:23 'sanctify you completely'; John 17:19 'may be sanctified by the truth'; Rev 22:11 'let the holy continue to be holy'). This was the worker's own fallback, kept in the first report.

rows.label: Every other use
